hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 adheres more tightly to some recycling receptors than APOE3, impeding recycling.

paper.title: Interaction of sortilin with apolipoprotein E3 enables neurons to use long-chain fatty acids as alternative metabolic fuel.

findings.finding_description: iPSC-derived human cortical neurons (NGN2) that were APOE ε4/ε4 and SORT1 wild-type (E4WT) were cultured with conditioned medium from E4WT astrocytes. Their maximal respiration fell with UK5099 but not with etomoxir, the same as SORT1-knockout neurons (E3KO) and unlike E3WT neurons. This phenocopy of sortilin loss is a surrogate readout for apoE4-disrupted sortilin function. Receptor binding and recycling were not measured.
findings.quote: By contrast, maximal respiration in E3KO iNs (Fig. 4b and Supplementary Fig. 8b), E4WT iNs (Fig. 4c and Supplementary Fig. 8c) or E4KO iNs (Fig. 4d and Supplementary Fig. 8d) was reduced by UK5099 but not by etomoxir.
findings.summary: In human iPSC neurons, apoE4 with intact sortilin phenocopies SORT1 knockout, losing sensitivity of respiration to LCFA-import blockade.
findings.experimental_system: iPSC-derived human NGN2 cortical neurons (APOE3/APOE4 × SORT1 WT/KO) with isogenic astrocyte-conditioned medium

findings.finding_description: E4WT human iNs were exposed to conditioned medium from either E4WT or E3WT iPSC astrocytes for 8 days. Etomoxir sensitivity of maximal respiration was restored only with E3WT astrocyte medium. This indicates that the apoE isoform supplied, not the neuron's genotype, determines the sortilin-dependent phenotype. The authors interpret this as apoE4 binding disrupting sortilin, but neither binding nor recycling was measured.
findings.quote: However, sensitivity to etomoxir was restored in E4WT iNs when exposed to medium conditioned by E3WT iAs (Fig. 4f,g and Supplementary Fig. 10b).
findings.summary: Supplying apoE3 rather than apoE4 to apoE4 human neurons rescues the sortilin-dependent ability to use LCFAs.
findings.experimental_system: iPSC-derived human E4WT neurons treated with E3WT vs E4WT iPSC-astrocyte conditioned medium

findings.finding_description: In human iNs, combining SORT1 knockout with APOE4 (E4KO) gave the same etomoxir-insensitive phenotype as E4WT, with no additive effect. This epistasis is consistent with apoE4 acting through loss of sortilin function. It does not show binding affinity or recycling.
findings.quote: Jointly, our findings in mouse and human cell models corroborated our hypothesis that genetic (E3KO, E4KO) or functional (E4WT) deficiency of sortilin disrupts the ability of neurons to support mitochondrial energy homeostasis through LCFA consumption.
findings.summary: ApoE4 and SORT1 loss are non-additive in human neurons, consistent with apoE4 acting via sortilin.

findings.finding_description: Cortical synaptosomes from 12-week-old humanized APOE knock-in mice were treated with UK5099 or etomoxir. Those from E4WT, E3KO and E4KO mice responded to UK5099 but not to etomoxir, whereas E3WT synaptosomes responded to both. This is a surrogate for apoE4-induced functional sortilin deficiency in young, non-AD mouse neurons, not human cells.
findings.quote: By contrast, synaptosomal mitochondria from E3KO (Fig. 1h and Supplementary Fig. 2b), E4WT (Fig. 1i and Supplementary Fig. 2c) and E4KO (Fig. 1j and Supplementary Fig. 2d) were sensitive to treatment with UK5099 but failed to respond to etomoxir.
findings.summary: In young humanized mouse synaptosomes, apoE4 phenocopies sortilin knockout in losing LCFA-dependent respiration.
findings.experimental_system: cortical synaptosomes from 12-week-old human APOE3/APOE4 targeted-replacement mice, Sort1 WT/KO

findings.finding_description: Under normal glucose, maximal respiration of synaptosomes from E3WT mice was significantly higher than from E3KO, E4WT or E4KO mice. The latter three genotypes did not differ from each other, consistent with apoE4 causing functional sortilin deficiency.
findings.quote: we identified a significantly higher maximal respiration in E3WT as compared to E3KO, E4WT or E4KO synaptosomes, with no statistically significant differences between the latter three genotypes
findings.summary: ApoE4 mouse synaptosomes match Sort1-KO in reduced maximal respiration.
findings.experimental_system: cortical synaptosomes from 12-week-old male humanized APOE knock-in mice, Sort1 WT/KO

findings.finding_description: Under low glucose, palmitate supplementation increased maximal respiration in E3WT synaptosomes but not in E3KO, E4WT or E4KO synaptosomes.
findings.quote: No increase in maximal respiration was seen in E3KO (Fig. 2c and Supplementary Fig. 4b), E4WT (Fig. 2d and Supplementary Fig. 4c) or E4KO (Fig. 2e and Supplementary Fig. 4d) synaptosomes after palmitate supplementation.
findings.summary: ApoE4 mouse synaptosomes cannot use palmitate as fuel, like Sort1-KO.
findings.experimental_system: cortical synaptosomes from 12-week-old male humanized APOE knock-in mice, Sort1 WT/KO

findings.finding_description: Synaptosomes were deprived of glucose and supplied only palmitate as fuel. Respiration was sustained in E3WT synaptosomes but shut down completely in E3KO, E4WT and E4KO synaptosomes.
findings.quote: In these experiments, mitochondrial respiration sustained in E3WT synaptosomes, but shut down completely in the three other genotypes
findings.summary: With palmitate as the sole fuel, apoE4 and Sort1-KO mouse synaptosomes fail to respire.
findings.experimental_system: cortical synaptosomes from 12-week-old male humanized APOE knock-in mice, Sort1 WT/KO

findings.finding_description: RT-qPCR on FACS-sorted neurons and astrocytes from the four mouse genotypes showed an APOE × Sort1 genotype interaction only in neurons, for Acadl, Crat and Cpt1a. This is consistent with an apoE4-sortilin interaction affecting neurons specifically.
findings.quote: However, an interaction of APOE and Sort1 genotypes on transcript levels was only seen in neurons and included the fatty acid oxidation enzyme long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase Acadl, and the carnitine acyltransferases Crat and Cpt1a (Fig. 3c).
findings.summary: ApoE4 and Sort1 loss converge on neuronal fatty-acid oxidation gene expression in mice.
findings.experimental_system: FACS-sorted neurons and astrocytes from 12-week-old male humanized APOE knock-in mice, Sort1 WT/KO

findings.finding_description: Short-chain fatty acids (acetic or butyric acid) increased maximal respiration in E3KO, E4WT and E4KO synaptosomes but not in E3WT synaptosomes. ApoE4 again grouped with sortilin loss, though this is a downstream metabolic surrogate.
findings.quote: Addition of either acetic acid or butyric acid significantly increased maximal respiration in E3KO (Fig. 2g and Supplementary Fig. 5b), E4WT (Fig. 2h and Supplementary Fig. 5c) and E4KO (Fig. 2i and Supplementary Fig. 5d), whereas no effect was seen in E3WT
findings.summary: ApoE4 mouse synaptosomes share the Sort1-KO metabolic shift toward short-chain fatty acid use.
findings.experimental_system: cortical synaptosomes from 12-week-old male humanized APOE knock-in mice, Sort1 WT/KO

findings.finding_description: Control experiment: iPSC astrocytes of all four genotypes produced and secreted similar amounts of apoE, which rules out apoE quantity as the explanation for the isoform effects. Directness class 5 because this measures neither receptor binding nor recycling, nor any surrogate of them; it only controls for ligand amount.
findings.quote: Importantly, iAs of all four genotypes produced and secreted similar amounts of apoE variants as shown by comparative RT–qPCR (Extended Data Fig. 5c) and western blotting (Extended Data Fig. 5d).
findings.summary: ApoE3 and apoE4 secretion by human iPSC astrocytes is similar, so isoform effects are not due to apoE quantity.
findings.experimental_system: iPSC-derived human astrocytes (SOX9/NFIB-induced), APOE3/APOE4 × SORT1 WT/KO

findings.finding_description: Human E4WT iPSC-derived neurons regained sensitivity to the CPT1A inhibitor etomoxir when maintained in apoE3-containing astrocyte-conditioned medium, but not in apoE4-containing medium, indicating that extracellular apoE4 disrupts sortilin-dependent neuronal LCFA uptake.
findings.quote: These findings argue for loss of sortilin activity in the brain of APOE ε4 carriers, an assumption corroborated by rescue of sensitivity to etomoxir in E4WT iNs when exposed to apoE3-containing rather than apoE4-containing astrocyte media (Fig. 4e–g).
findings.summary: E4WT neurons recover LCFA fuel use with apoE3 but not apoE4 astrocyte medium.
findings.experimental_system: iPSC-derived human E4WT cortical neurons treated with conditioned medium from iPSC-derived human E3WT or E4WT astrocytes

findings.finding_description: CPT1A transcript and protein levels were significantly higher in E3WT iPSC-derived neurons than in E3KO, E4WT, or E4KO neurons, and the latter three genotypes did not differ significantly from one another.
findings.quote: Levels of CPT1A transcript (Fig. 6e) and CPT1A protein (Fig. 6f,g) were significantly higher in E3WT as compared to E3KO, E4WT or E4KO iNs, with no statistically significant difference between the latter three genotypes.
findings.summary: E4WT and E4KO neurons phenocopy SORT1-null neurons in CPT1A expression.
findings.experimental_system: iPSC-derived human cortical neurons of APOE ε3/ε3 or ε4/ε4 and SORT1 WT or KO genotypes treated with iPSC-derived astrocyte-conditioned medium

findings.finding_description: In APOE ε4/ε4 human iPSC-derived neurons, SORT1 deletion did not further alter most PUFA and eCB levels relative to SORT1-intact E4WT neurons, implying that apoE4 already renders neurons functionally sortilin-deficient.
findings.quote: Importantly, SORT1 deficiency did not alter the concentrations of most PUFAs and eCBs in E4KO iNs when compared with isogenic E4WT neurons (Extended Data Fig. 9), a finding in agreement with apoE4 rendering WT neurons functionally deficient for sortilin.
findings.summary: SORT1 knockout has no added effect on neuronal lipids in an apoE4 background.
findings.experimental_system: iPSC-derived human E4WT and E4KO cortical neurons cultured with isogenic astrocyte-conditioned medium

findings.finding_description: Transcription profiles of 84 PPAR target genes showed no additional effect of SORT1 deficiency when comparing E4KO and E4WT human iPSC-derived neurons, supporting functional inactivation of sortilin in the presence of apoE4.
findings.quote: Importantly, no effect of sortilin deficiency on any of the above genes was seen comparing transcription profiles in E4KO and E4WT iNs, corroborating functional sortilin deficiency in the presence of apoE4 (Extended Data Fig. 10).
findings.summary: SORT1 deletion does not further change PPAR target gene expression in apoE4 neurons.
findings.experimental_system: iPSC-derived human E4WT and E4KO cortical neurons

findings.finding_description: Pharmacological activation of PPARα with bezafibrate restored etomoxir sensitivity in E4WT and E4KO human iPSC-derived neurons, showing that the apoE4-associated mitochondrial phenotype can be rescued downstream of sortilin.
findings.quote: Similarly to the situation in E3KO, bezafibrate treatment also increased PPARα activity in E4WT and E4KO iNs (Fig. 7d,g) and established sensitivity to etomoxir (Fig. 7e,f,h,i and Supplementary Figs. 12 and 13).
findings.summary: PPARα agonist rescues LCFA fuel use in E4WT and E4KO neurons.
findings.experimental_system: iPSC-derived human E4WT and E4KO cortical neurons treated with 100 µM bezafibrate

findings.finding_description: Conditioned media from apoE3-expressing and apoE4-expressing human iPSC-derived astrocytes contained comparable levels of LCFA, PUFA, and eCB precursors, arguing that observed neuronal phenotypes are not due to differential lipid availability.
findings.quote: However, LCFA, PUFA and eCB precursors showed comparable levels in media conditioned by apoE3 (Fig. 5b) or apoE4 (Extended Data Fig. 9b) expressing WT astrocytes.
findings.summary: E3 and E4 astrocyte-conditioned media have similar LCFA/PUFA/eCB precursor levels.
findings.experimental_system: iPSC-derived human E3WT and E4WT astrocyte-conditioned medium
